cold_open: Tom scored 138.85, the best Week 5 score in league history and the sixth-best of 3,992 scores ever. For the second straight week, a perfect lineup lost: Jeff started his best possible team, scored 103.13, and fell to Eric by 5.5.

notes.Kevin O'Boyle|Thomas: Tom beat his projection by 48.99, with the 49ers' 18.0 the defense of the week. The 61.13 margin was the week's biggest blowout. Tom has won five straight, tying the series record, and leads 17–14.
notes.Eric|Jeff: The unluckiest loss: Jeff's lineup was perfect and his 103.13 was fourth-best. Drake Maye's 38.73, the quarterback of the week for the second week running, gave Eric a career-high 108.63 and a 3–2 lead.
notes.Brian Clark|Evan: Evan's best possible lineup scored 115.7 and wins it: Isaiah Likely's 22.2 sat on the bench behind Mike Washington Jr.'s 1.0 at flex. Clark has won two straight and trails 15–14.
notes.Fadi|Kevin Swanson: The week's narrowest win, by 2.7, and the luckiest: Fadi's 83.22 was only eighth-best. Jameson Williams's 15.35 sat on Swanson's bench behind Tee Higgins's 2.1. Fadi has won two straight; Swanson leads 16–14.
notes.Douglas|Shawn: Doug was projected for 82.54 and scored 56.25, 26.29 under: the furthest below projection in the league. Shawn's 97.97 was fifth-best, with Trey McBride's 13.8 the tight end of the week. Shawn leads 9–4.
notes.Dominic|Steve Swanson: Dominic's 55.31 was the week's low, short of all eleven other teams. Steve started his best possible lineup, led by Christian Watson's 22.15, the receiver of the week. Dominic leads 15–13.

kicker: In Week 3, Tyler Shough was the quarterback of the week, 24.9 for Kevin O'Boyle. This week he was the dud: −2.08 on a 13.61 projection, with C.J. Stroud's 17.47 on O'Boyle's bench.
